chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a person in ihram who killed an ostrich.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a camel. If he cannot find one, then feeding sixty poor people; he does not exceed feeding sixty poor people. If the value of the camel is less than the cost of feeding sixty poor people, then there is upon him only the value of the camel.'

If he is unable to feed sixty poor people and cannot fast for the number of days equal to what he feeds each poor person for one day, then let him fast eighteen days and there is nothing upon him. And likewise for the cow and the wild donkey, he fasts nine days, and for the gazelle and what resembles it, three days.
This is if he is unable to feed and unable to fast for the number of days equal to the ransom price of each poor person for one day.
As for with the ability to do that, then there is for him only that. And that which indicates its permissibility in case of necessity is what has been narrated:

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A mature camel, used here as the primary unit of compensation
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation (kaffarah) for killing game while in the state of ihram during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the graduated fidya for killing game while in ihram, prioritizing the value of a camel (badanah) or feeding sixty poor people, with fasting as a fallback for those unable to afford food. It distinguishes between the compensation for larger game (eighteen days of fasting) and smaller game (nine or three days), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on proportional expiation based on the animal's size and the pilgrim's financial capacity. The text also notes that these specific durations apply when one cannot provide the daily food equivalent for each poor person, highlighting the flexibility within Shia fiqh for cases of necessity.
